# Selected technical work

This page brings together software projects and scientific publications. Each item is linked to a public source that can be inspected independently.

## Scientific publications

### Reduced-Order Modelling of Dispersion (2008)

**Jean-Marc Brun and Bijan Mohammadi**  
Book chapter in *Partial Differential Equations: Modelling and Numerical Simulation*, pp. 245–256.

The chapter presents low-complexity models for passive-scalar transport and dispersion in environmental applications. The approach combines reduced-dimensional solution spaces, similarity solutions, data assimilation, and sensitivity analysis. It is designed to estimate concentrations without solving a full PDE over the entire domain.

- [Chapter record — Springer](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-1-4020-8758-5_14)
- [Book record — Springer](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4020-8758-5)

### Similitude généralisée et modélisation géométrique à complexité réduite (2006)

**Bijan Mohammadi and Jean-Marc Brun**  
*Comptes Rendus. Mécanique*, 334(10), 634–638. DOI: 10.1016/j.crme.2006.06.007.

This paper presents a reduced-complexity model for passive-scalar transport and dispersion in environmental applications. It develops similarity solutions in a non-symmetric metric based on transport times and uses partial observational data for model identification. The method is mesh-free and can estimate the solution at a point without computing the full spatial field.

- [Publisher record and abstract — Comptes Rendus. Mécanique](https://comptes-rendus.academie-sciences.fr/mecanique/articles/10.1016/j.crme.2006.06.007/)
- [Alternative bibliographic record — Semantic Scholar](https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Similitude-g%C3%A9n%C3%A9ralis%C3%A9e-et-mod%C3%A9lisation-g%C3%A9om%C3%A9trique-Mohammadi-Brun/16f7bdf72d12165abf39078f4078438162304fbe)

These two publications are related outputs on reduced-order modelling and environmental dispersion. The publisher records are the primary references.

### Contribution to a public-health exposure study (2006)

**Évaluation de l’exposition aérienne aux pesticides de la population générale — Étude en air extérieur dans quatre sites de l’Hérault en 2006**

The report by the French public-health surveillance institute (Institut de veille sanitaire, now part of Santé publique France) examines pesticide concentrations in outdoor air at four sites in Hérault and discusses population exposure. Jean-Marc Brun is listed in the report among the people who also participated in the study; the report does not specify an individual role or contribution.

- [Study report (PDF)](https://www.santepubliquefrance.fr/sites/default/files/rdd/document/82748_9958-9958-ps.pdf)

## LLM hallucination evaluation benchmark

**Goal**

Compare approaches to detecting unsupported or hallucinated content in language-model outputs using an evaluation protocol that makes comparisons interpretable.

**Technical work**

- Integration of multiple fact-checking and evaluation systems
- Metric calculation and aggregation from predictions
- Threshold analysis and trade-offs between metrics
- Streamlit visualisation of benchmark results and errors
- Modular code and tests for calculation components

**What it demonstrates**

Evaluation engineering: defining labels and units of analysis, checking metric validity, and distinguishing supported conclusions from claims the data cannot justify.

**Repository status**

A public repository URL, shareable datasets, full protocol, and numerical results have not yet been verified. No repository link or benchmark result is claimed here.

## LLM Wiki — building a source-grounded knowledge base

**Goal**

Turn documentary sources into a structured, searchable, maintainable knowledge base while preserving traceability to source material.

**Technical work**

- Source ingestion and organisation
- Generation of knowledge pages from documents
- Structural validation and consistency checks
- Search across generated knowledge
- Automation and integration of checks into the development workflow

**What it demonstrates**

Knowledge engineering for LLM-based systems: provenance, validation, maintainability, and treating generated content as an engineering artefact rather than trusting generation alone.

**Repository**

[Wiki Knowledge on GitHub](https://github.com/JM-Brun/wiki-knowledge)

The repository contains the implementation and project documentation. Its current state and limitations should be reviewed alongside the code.
